---
title: "Layout Modeling Check"
description: "Check from a layout repository that a Palace simulation can model a layout, before any simulation is set up."
scgsim-kind: "contract"
scgsim-status: "CONVERGING"
scgsim-id: "docs/layout-modeling-check"
---

Each Palace simulation class has a class-level `simulation_drc()` that tells a
layout repository whether that simulation can model its layout. It runs the
same preparation and geometry build that the class's `mesh()` runs, then stops
before meshing. A layout that cannot be modeled is refused with the error the
build raises, and a layout that can be modeled returns `None`.

The check catches layout defects that stop modeling: malformed shapes,
overlaps, tiny misalignments, wrong semantic declarations, port sheets that do
not sit where they should, and Surface EPR bands that do not fit the drawn
gaps. It does not predict the final simulation geometry. The patterns SCGSim is
tested on are listed in [Supported Geometry](supported-geometry.qmd), and the
known failures with their layout fixes in
[Known Geometry Problems](known-geometry-problems.qmd). The rules the check
enforces, and who owns each failure, are on [Supported Scope](supported-scope.qmd).

## Call the check of each simulation the layout is for

`EigenmodeSim` selects and numbers the authored port sheets and
`ElectrostaticSim` does not, so the two have separate checks. A component meant
for an Eigenmode simulation calls `EigenmodeSim.simulation_drc`; one meant for
both calls both.

The check needs the layout Component and the PDK data a simulation would use:
the layer stack and the material records. SCGSim does not depend on a PDK, so
the layout repository passes them in. It needs `scgsim[palace]` installed.

```python
from scgsim.palace import EigenmodeSim, ElectrostaticSim


def test_the_layout_can_be_modeled():
    for simulation in (EigenmodeSim, ElectrostaticSim):
        simulation.simulation_drc(
            component,
            layer_stack=layer_stack,
            material_records=material_records,
            nets=nets,
            surface_epr_specs=surface_epr_specs,
        )
```

Call it from the repository's tests and while the layout is being drawn. Pass
`surface_epr_specs` with the specs the simulations will use: they are the ones
[`set_surface_epr`](specs/palace-eigenmode.qmd#surface-epr-margins) takes, and
their margins are cut into the geometry as bands, so a layout that cannot carry
them is refused here too. Bands are cut only on the faces the specs select, so
a layout with no such face passes with no bands. For an assembly, pass
`instances` as `{"chip/device": reference, ...}`, as
`GeometryPlan.register_instance` takes them; the plan's root is named `chip`.
They are registered in the mapping's order, so list a parent before its
children (`chip/device` before `chip/device/pads`).

Pass `nets` with the Net assignment the simulation's plan is given, in the form
`GeometryPlan.set_nets` takes: `{"Ground": ("chip/D0_TOP_GROUND_PLANE", ...),
...}`, with each member a qualified Entity ID under `chip`. The check then
builds the model that simulation builds. Without `nets` no conductor has a Net,
so any two conductors that touch are refused as a different-Net contact. That
refuses every flip-chip layout whose indium bumps join the two ground planes,
until both planes and every bump are given as one Ground net. A contact between
conductors of two different Nets is refused with or without `nets`.

The check builds the geometry and does not mesh or solve, so it can be repeated
as the layout changes. It stops at the first refusal. Read the message, fix the
layout, and run it again. The [error archive](errors.qmd) records diagnostics
seen in practice.

A refusal can also come from a defect in SGB rather than from the layout. If
the message does not match the layout you drew, report it to SCGSim.

## What the check uses

The settings are fixed:

- Route B and Palace's default airbox;
- a 1 µm vacuum region on all six faces when the layout has no vacuum of its
  own, and the layout's own vacuum when it has one, so the metal has air faces
  for `MA` and `SA` bands;
- zero coupon padding;
- the Net assignment given as `nets`, and no Net when it is not given;
- for `EigenmodeSim`, every authored port with a fixed inductance, which does
  not change the geometry;
- for `ElectrostaticSim`, no terminals, and an empty Surface EPR when
  `surface_epr_specs` is not given, because `mesh()` requires Surface EPR.

`simulation_drc()` writes into a temporary folder and removes it. It adds no
rules of its own and no report type, so the error is the one that class's
`mesh()` raises for the same layout and settings.

::: {.callout-note title="What a pass means"}
A pass means the model built with the fixed settings above was accepted; it
does not say how many bands were cut. It does not promise that other settings will model: Route A,
Electrostatic terminals, junctions, lumped supports, indium bumps or a
different vacuum region. To check a specific set-up, run that simulation's own `mesh()`.
:::

AEDT is outside this check: its STEP import is not covered yet.
